title: Sinusitis
summary: Only prescribe an antibiotic immediately if patient is systemically very unwell, or has symptoms and signs of a more serious illness or condition, or has high risk of complications.
changeSummary: Initial transcription from Eolas Medical, Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial Guidelines (v5.119.0).
clinicalNotes: Non-serious symptoms <10 days: No antibiotic, as most cases resolve in 14 days without.

For symptoms > 10 days: No antibiotic or delayed antibiotic depending on likelihood of bacterial cause. Consider high-dose nasal corticosteroid for 14 days (off-label use) if symptomatic for 10 days+ and aged 12 years+ (NICE NG79).
Systemically very unwell, or more serious signs and symptoms, or high risk of complications: Immediate antibiotic.

specialConsiderations.title: Second-line and allergy
items: Consult local microbiologist for alternative second choice in penicillin allergy, or worsening symptoms on second choice taken for at least 2 to 3 days.

specialConsiderations.title: Referral
items: Refer 'red flags' to secondary care, including: unilateral signs (e.g. unilateral polyps or mass); bleeding; diplopia or proptosis; orbital swelling or erythema; suspicion of intracranial complication; immunocompromised patient.
